package_info.package_versions: All observed variants since November 2023 (e.g., e346f6b36569d7b8c52a55403a6b78ae0ed15c0aaae4011490404bdb04ff28e5, ae2a5a02d0ef173b1d38a26c5a88b796f4ee2e8f36ee00931c468cd496fb2b5a, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: Emansrepo is a Python-based infostealer distributed via phishing emails. It exfiltrates sensitive browser data, files, credentials, crypto wallets, and cookies to attacker-controlled email addresses. The malware is delivered through multi-stage loaders and deletes evidence after exfiltration, demonstrating clear intent to steal and evade detection.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after user opens malicious attachment and payload is executed)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Collects login data, credit card info, web history, download history, autofill, and text files (<0.2MB) from Desktop, Documents, Downloads. Saves to %TEMP%\Browsers\{browser name}\ as Saved_Passwords.txt, Saved_Credit_Cards.txt, Browser_History.txt, Download_History.txt, Autofill_Data.txt. Compresses %TEMP%\Browsers and emails as attachment to minestealer8412@maternamedical[.]top.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates browser data and text files, writes them to a temporary directory, compresses the directory, and sends the archive as an email attachment to an attacker-controlled address, enabling credential and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting browser credentials, credit cards, and personal files, then exfiltrating them via email is a hallmark of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or exfiltrate browser credentials or user files without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise backup or migration tools may access browser data, but never exfiltrate it to untrusted email addresses.
key_indicators: Bulk access to browser credential stores
Automated email exfiltration to hardcoded attacker address
Temporary storage and deletion of stolen data

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after initial data theft, as part of staged execution)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Copies PDF files (<0.1MB) from Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Recents. Compresses browser extension, crypto wallet, and game platform data folders into zip files. Stores all in %TEMP%\pdf_temps and emails to filelogs@maternamedical[.]top.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects PDF documents and sensitive data from browser extensions, crypto wallets, and game platforms, compresses them, and exfiltrates the data via email to an attacker-controlled address.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Targeting crypto wallets, browser extensions, and game platform data is a clear sign of financially motivated malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not access or compress wallet or extension data for exfiltration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup utilities may compress user data, but not send it to unknown email addresses.
key_indicators: Access to crypto wallet and browser extension directories
Compression and exfiltration of sensitive data
Use of multiple attacker-controlled email addresses

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Copies browser cookie files, compresses them into {process_name}_cookies.zip in %TEMP%\cookies_data, and emails the zip files to cooklielogs@maternamedical[.]top.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code locates browser cookie files, compresses them, and exfiltrates the archive via email to an attacker-controlled address, enabling session hijacking.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Stealing browser cookies enables account/session hijacking and is a common infostealer tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or exfiltrate browser cookies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Browser sync features may access cookies, but not exfiltrate them externally.
key_indicators: Bulk access to browser cookie files
Compression and exfiltration to attacker email

execution_context.file_location: AutoIt script in Purchase-Order.exe or PowerShell script (script.ps1) in chain 1/2

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Downloads preoffice.zip to %TEMP%, extracts to %TEMP%\PythonTemp, and executes tester.py (the infostealer payload).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At postinstall, the code downloads a secondary payload (preoffice.zip), extracts it, and executes the main infostealer script, enabling staged malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing secondary payloads is a classic malware staging technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers should not download and execute unverified code from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download updates, but from trusted sources and with user consent.
key_indicators: Silent download and execution of remote payloads
Use of temp directories for staging

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with malicious attachment (HTML, HTA, or 7z archive).
Dropper (AutoIt, PowerShell, or batch file) downloads and extracts preoffice.zip containing the Python infostealer.
Infostealer (tester.py) executes, harvesting browser credentials, files, and other sensitive data.
Stolen data is compressed and exfiltrated via email to attacker-controlled addresses. Temporary folders are deleted to cover tracks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen data for further exploitation

behavioral_signatures: Bulk access to browser credential stores and cookie files
Automated compression and exfiltration of user data via email
Silent download and execution of secondary payloads from remote servers
Temporary storage and deletion of stolen data in %TEMP% directories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes accessing browser credential stores, cookies, and crypto wallet directories in bulk, especially if followed by compression and outbound SMTP/email activity to suspicious domains. Flag downloads and execution of secondary payloads from untrusted remote sources, and watch for creation and rapid deletion of temp directories containing sensitive data. Correlate with known IOCs and email addresses used for exfiltration.
